correctness.rationale: The two explicit isomorphic graph models have the same 27 edges and 18 vertices. Bitmask and set-based exhaustive signatures agree on all optimal cardinalities, code counts and exchange components. All 18,564 six-set LD candidates, 48,620 nine-set ID candidates, and 126 five-choices on each OLD bipartition side were covered, with smaller sizes excluded by proofs or complete enumeration. The LD/OLD incidence lower bounds, Cartesian-factor argument, and factor BFS calculations were reconstructed and verified from packaged program paths. No numerical experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The canonical Pappus incidence graph exhibits a sharply contrasted reconfiguration hierarchy across three standard sensor-location formulations: isolated minimum LD codes, two invariant ID families, and a connected OLD family. Exact 45-configuration factor geometry and Cartesian-square radius/diameter identify why the open-neighborhood case is globally navigable; the majority-side criterion identifies the ID obstruction. These are motivated complete optimal-configuration classifications, not arbitrary numerical slices or routine restatements of published cubic bounds.
